Yes. 0.999... is the limit of 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, ..., and that limit is exactly 1. The gap after n nines is 10⁻ⁿ, which falls below any positive number you name, so the gap is zero.

Quick check: 1/3 = 0.333..., so 3 × (1/3) = 0.999... and also = 1.

The apparent paradox comes from treating 0.999... as a number that "keeps approaching" 1. The notation names the limit itself, not the sequence of steps toward it.
